q: Which 3 music genres generated the most sales revenue (the amount customers paid for tracks of that genre)?
wrong:
SELECT g.Name AS genre, SUM(i.Total) AS revenue
FROM Invoice i
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.Name
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 3
right:
SELECT g.Name AS genre, SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS revenue
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.Name
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 3
mistake: Sums the invoice-level Total after joining to invoice lines, so each invoice total is counted once per line (join fan-out) and attributed to every genre on the invoice.

q: How many employees have nobody reporting to them (i.e. are not the manager of any other employee)?
wrong:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS employees_without_reports
FROM Employee
WHERE EmployeeId NOT IN (SELECT ReportsTo FROM Employee)
right:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS employees_without_reports
FROM Employee
WHERE EmployeeId NOT IN (SELECT ReportsTo FROM Employee WHERE ReportsTo IS NOT NULL)
mistake: NOT IN against a subquery that contains a NULL (the General Manager's ReportsTo) is never true, so the count is 0.

q: What percentage of tracks in the catalog are video tracks (media type 'Protected MPEG-4 video file')? Round to 2 decimals.
wrong:
SELECT ROUND(100 * SUM(CASE WHEN m.Name = 'Protected MPEG-4 video file' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_video
FROM Track t
JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId
right:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN m.Name = 'Protected MPEG-4 video file' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_video
FROM Track t
JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId
mistake: All operands are integers, so the division truncates and the percentage loses its decimals (6.0 instead of 6.11).

q: On average, how many albums does an artist have, across all artists in the Artist table (artists with no albums count as 0)?
wrong:
SELECT AVG(album_count) AS avg_albums_per_artist
FROM (
  SELECT ar.ArtistId, COUNT(*) AS album_count
  FROM Artist ar
  LEFT JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
  GROUP BY ar.ArtistId
)
right:
SELECT AVG(album_count) AS avg_albums_per_artist
FROM (
  SELECT ar.ArtistId, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS album_count
  FROM Artist ar
  LEFT JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
  GROUP BY ar.ArtistId
)
mistake: COUNT(*) after a LEFT JOIN counts the NULL-padded row, so artists with no albums are counted as having 1 album.

q: How much revenue has the store earned from selling Jazz tracks?
wrong:
SELECT SUM(t.UnitPrice) AS jazz_revenue
FROM Track t
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Jazz'
right:
SELECT SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS jazz_revenue
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Jazz'
mistake: Sums catalog list prices of all Jazz tracks (the value of the catalog) instead of what was actually sold on invoice lines.

q: How many customers are not located in California (State = 'CA')? Include customers in countries where no state is recorded.
wrong:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_outside_ca
FROM Customer
WHERE State <> 'CA'
right:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_outside_ca
FROM Customer
WHERE State IS NULL OR State <> 'CA'
mistake: State <> 'CA' evaluates to NULL for customers with no state, silently dropping 29 customers.

q: What is the average lifetime amount a customer has spent at the store?
wrong:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(Total), 2) AS avg_spend_per_customer
FROM Invoice
right:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(customer_total), 2) AS avg_spend_per_customer
FROM (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS customer_total
      FROM Invoice
      GROUP BY CustomerId)
mistake: Averages individual invoice totals (average order value) rather than each customer's summed lifetime spend.

q: What is the total invoiced revenue from the customers assigned to each sales support agent?
wrong:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS agent, SUM(i.Total) AS revenue
FROM Employee e
JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = e.EmployeeId
JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId
ORDER BY revenue DESC
right:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS agent, SUM(i.Total) AS revenue
FROM Employee e
JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId
ORDER BY revenue DESC
mistake: Joins Customer to Employee on CustomerId = EmployeeId instead of SupportRepId, pairing each employee with an unrelated customer.

q: How many orders were placed in calendar year 2021?
wrong:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_2021
FROM Orders
WHERE OrderDate BETWEEN '2021-01-01' AND '2021-12-31'
right:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_2021
FROM Orders
WHERE OrderDate >= '2021-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2022-01-01'
mistake: OrderDate includes a time of day, so BETWEEN ... '2021-12-31' excludes orders placed later on December 31.

q: What is the total net sales revenue (after discounts) from 'Raclette Courdavault' across all orders?
wrong:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS net_revenue
FROM [Order Details] od
JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
WHERE p.ProductName = 'Raclette Courdavault'
right:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS net_revenue
FROM [Order Details] od
JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
WHERE p.ProductName = 'Raclette Courdavault'
mistake: Uses the product's current list price (Products.UnitPrice) instead of the price actually charged on each order line.

q: How many orders shipped with Speedy Express or United Package had a freight charge above 500?
wrong:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS heavy_freight_orders
FROM Orders o
JOIN Shippers s ON s.ShipperID = o.ShipVia
WHERE s.CompanyName = 'Speedy Express' OR s.CompanyName = 'United Package' AND o.Freight > 500
right:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS heavy_freight_orders
FROM Orders o
JOIN Shippers s ON s.ShipperID = o.ShipVia
WHERE (s.CompanyName = 'Speedy Express' OR s.CompanyName = 'United Package') AND o.Freight > 500
mistake: AND binds tighter than OR, so the freight filter only applies to United Package and every Speedy Express order is counted.

q: How many products come from suppliers based in Sweden?
wrong:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS swedish_products
FROM Products p
JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID
WHERE s.Country = 'Sweden'
right:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS swedish_products
FROM Products p
JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID
WHERE TRIM(s.Country) = 'Sweden'
mistake: Exact string match misses a supplier whose Country is stored as 'Sweden ' with a trailing space.

q: Which 3 countries have the most orders, based on the country where the ordering customer is located?
wrong:
SELECT ShipCountry AS country, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY ShipCountry
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 3
right:
SELECT c.Country AS country, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM Orders o
JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
GROUP BY c.Country
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 3
mistake: Groups by the shipping destination country on the order rather than the customer's own country, which differ for most orders.

q: For each manager, how many employees report directly to them?
wrong:
SELECT m.FirstName || ' ' || m.LastName AS manager, COUNT(*) AS direct_reports
FROM Employees e
JOIN Employees m ON e.EmployeeID = m.ReportsTo
GROUP BY m.EmployeeID
ORDER BY direct_reports DESC
right:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS manager, COUNT(*) AS direct_reports
FROM Employees e
JOIN Employees m ON e.EmployeeID = m.ReportsTo
GROUP BY e.EmployeeID
ORDER BY direct_reports DESC
mistake: The self-join roles are swapped: it groups by the subordinate (m) instead of the manager (e), so every employee shows 1 report.

q: What was the total freight charged on orders placed in 2019 that contained at least one Beverages product?
wrong:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(o.Freight), 2) AS total_freight
FROM Orders o
JOIN [Order Details] od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
WHERE c.CategoryName = 'Beverages'
  AND o.OrderDate >= '2019-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2020-01-01'
right:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(o.Freight), 2) AS total_freight
FROM Orders o
WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2019-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2020-01-01'
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1
              FROM [Order Details] od
              JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
              JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
              WHERE od.OrderID = o.OrderID AND c.CategoryName = 'Beverages')
mistake: Order-level Freight is summed once per matching beverage line, so orders with several beverage products have their freight counted multiple times.

q: How many active (not discontinued) products need to be reordered? A product needs reordering when the stock it will have, counting units already on order, is at or below its reorder level.
wrong:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_to_reorder
FROM Products
WHERE Discontinued = '0'
  AND UnitsInStock <= ReorderLevel
right:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_to_reorder
FROM Products
WHERE Discontinued = '0'
  AND UnitsInStock + UnitsOnOrder <= ReorderLevel
mistake: Compares only units in stock to the reorder level and ignores units already on order, so products that are being replenished are flagged.

q: Which actor has appeared in the most films, and in how many films?
wrong:
SELECT a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS actor, COUNT(*) AS films
FROM actor a
JOIN film_actor fa ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id
GROUP BY a.first_name, a.last_name
ORDER BY films DESC
LIMIT 1
right:
SELECT a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS actor, COUNT(*) AS films
FROM actor a
JOIN film_actor fa ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id
GROUP BY a.actor_id
ORDER BY films DESC
LIMIT 1
mistake: Groups by actor name instead of actor_id, merging the two different actors named SUSAN DAVIS into one person with 54 films.

q: In February 2006, what was the average number of rentals per customer, across all customers (customers with no rentals that month count as 0)?
wrong:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(n), 3) AS avg_rentals_per_customer
FROM (
  SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(r.rental_id) AS n
  FROM customer c
  LEFT JOIN rental r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
  WHERE r.rental_date >= '2006-02-01' AND r.rental_date < '2006-03-01'
  GROUP BY c.customer_id
)
right:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(n), 3) AS avg_rentals_per_customer
FROM (
  SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(r.rental_id) AS n
  FROM customer c
  LEFT JOIN rental r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
                    AND r.rental_date >= '2006-02-01' AND r.rental_date < '2006-03-01'
  GROUP BY c.customer_id
)
mistake: Filtering the right-hand table in WHERE turns the LEFT JOIN into an inner join, so customers with zero rentals are dropped from the average.

q: How many different films were rented at least once in July 2005?
wrong:
SELECT COUNT(i.film_id) AS films_rented
FROM rental r
JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
WHERE r.rental_date >= '2005-07-01' AND r.rental_date < '2005-08-01'
right:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.film_id) AS films_rented
FROM rental r
JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
WHERE r.rental_date >= '2005-07-01' AND r.rental_date < '2005-08-01'
mistake: Counts rental rows instead of distinct films (missing DISTINCT), so a film rented many times is counted many times.

q: What is the average number of inventory copies per film, across all films in the catalog (films with no copies count as 0)?
wrong:
SELECT AVG(copies) AS avg_copies_per_film
FROM (
  SELECT f.film_id, COUNT(*) AS copies
  FROM film f
  LEFT JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.film_id
)
right:
SELECT AVG(copies) AS avg_copies_per_film
FROM (
  SELECT f.film_id, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies
  FROM film f
  LEFT JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.film_id
)
mistake: COUNT(*) on the LEFT JOIN counts the NULL row, so the 42 films with no inventory are counted as having one copy.

q: What was the total amount of payments received in July 2005?
wrong:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS july_payments
FROM payment
WHERE payment_date BETWEEN '2005-07-01' AND '2005-07-31'
right:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS july_payments
FROM payment
WHERE payment_date >= '2005-07-01' AND payment_date < '2005-08-01'
mistake: payment_date is a timestamp, so BETWEEN ... '2005-07-31' drops every payment made during July 31.

q: What is the total payment revenue from rentals of inventory held at store 2?
wrong:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.amount), 2) AS store2_revenue
FROM payment p
JOIN staff s ON s.staff_id = p.staff_id
WHERE s.store_id = 2
right:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.amount), 2) AS store2_revenue
FROM payment p
JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
WHERE i.store_id = 2
mistake: Attributes payments to the store of the staff member who took the payment, not the store that owns the rented inventory.

q: Which 3 film categories had the most rentals?
wrong:
SELECT c.name AS category, COUNT(*) AS rentals
FROM category c
JOIN film_category fc ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.name
ORDER BY rentals DESC
LIMIT 3
right:
SELECT c.name AS category, COUNT(*) AS rentals
FROM rental r
JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
JOIN film_category fc ON fc.film_id = i.film_id
JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id
GROUP BY c.name
ORDER BY rentals DESC
LIMIT 3
mistake: Counts the films in each category (catalog size) instead of the number of rentals.

q: Who are the top 3 customers by total amount paid?
wrong:
SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer, COUNT(p.payment_id) AS total
FROM customer c
JOIN payment p ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 3
right:
SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer, ROUND(SUM(p.amount), 2) AS total
FROM customer c
JOIN payment p ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 3
mistake: Ranks customers by number of payments instead of the sum of amounts paid.
